To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

size-tunable anatas TiO(2 )nanospindles were successfully prepared by a simple hydrothermal process, the TiO2 nanospindles can self-assemble onto GO via a spontaneous process, and the TiO2@TiO(x )N(y)/Ti N-GS nanocomposite shows excellent rate capability and cycle stability for rechargeable lithium-ion batteries.
size-tunable anatas TiO(2 )nanospindles were synthesized and assembled into anatase TiON/TiN-graphene nanocomposite for rechargeable lithium-ion batteries with high cycling stability.

the size-tunable anastase TiO( 2) nanospindle@titanium nitride/titanium oxynitrade-graphene (TiO( 2)-TiN/TiO( x)N( y)-GS) hybrid nanocomposites have been synthesized by using a simple two-step process.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of size-tunable Ti-based nanospindles by using a facile hydrothermal process and their assembly into a Ti-based nanocomposite for LIBs.

the synthesis and characterization of size-tunable Ti(IV) oxide nanospindles, their assembly onto graphene nanosheets to form TiO(2)-based hybrid nanocomposites, and their application as anode materials for LIBs.

the synthesis of anatase Ti(4+)O(2) (TiO(4+)) nanospindles from tubular titanate nanorods, their self-assembly onto graphene oxide sheets, and the subsequent nitridation of the TiO(n) surface and reduction of the graphene oxide sheets to yield anatase@Ti(4+)O(x)N(1-x)/TiN-graphene nanocomposite.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have successfully synthesized a novel TiO(2)-based nanomaterial with unique physicochemical properties by tuning the size and surface structure of anatase TiOnanospindles.
the TiO2@TiOxNy/TiN-GS nanospindles are promising anode materials for high-performance LIBs.

the anatase TiONy/TiN-GS nanohybrids with graphene nanosheet as the matrix and the TiO(3)@TiONy/TiNGS nanospindles as the active material are promising anode materials for LIBs with high rate capability, excellent cycling performance and good capacity retention.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a facile and effective method for synthesizing TiO(2)-based nanocomposites by combining hydrothermal synthesis, spontaneous self-assembly and thermal nitridation, which are promising anode materials for LIBs.

the size-tunable anastase nanospindles have been synthesized via a hydrothermal route by using tubular titantates as self-sacrficing precursors, which were then densely dispersed onto functional graphene oxdes via a spontaneous self-assemby process.

the synthesis of the size-tunable anatase TiO(2)-based nanomaterials and their functionalization into hybrid nanostructures with high surface area and high electronic conductivity are promising strategies to develop advanced anode materials for rechargeable LIBs with high energy density and high power density.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the TiO(x)N(1-x) shell on the TiO(1.5)N(0.5)@TiO(2)-GS nanocomposite not only improves the electronic conductivity of the TiO(x)-based nanospindles but also effectively prevents the TiO(0.5)/TiN core-shell structure from being oxidized during the cycling process.

the TiO(x)N/TiN-GS nanosheets with the TiO(x)/TiN nanocrystals on both sides can be considered as a promising conductive matrix for the assembly and functionalization of TiO(,2)-based nanocrystals to enhance their performance in various energy storage devices such as LIBs.

the size-tunable anisotropic TiO(2)-based nanostructures with their unique surface planes can be used as a versatile platform for the design and fabrication of advanced nanocomposites with superior performance in various energy storage and conversion applications.
